source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Yes, that's correct. The main board has:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor (on the 3.3V rail)
\- USB-C connector (programming port) + LDO for standalone operation
\- All the JST connectors (to power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch, LEDs, buttons, reset)
\- Support passives: decoupling caps, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, BOOT button

No sensors, no power management — those are on the other boards.

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module model.
The source identifies the main board as excluding power management but does not change the boost converter, its GPIO control, loads, or power-board behavior.
The candidate already has a same-message Event recording the button, reset, touch, and BOOT interfaces established by this source.
The source confirms the controller and connector inventory but specifies no GPIO assignment change.
The programming USB-C connector on the main board does not alter the previously established placement or accessibility of connectors on the power board.
The main-board inventory does not change the power board's dimensions, mounting, orientation, or charging-port edge placement.
The mention of the INA219 on the 3.3V rail is consistent with the existing DCDC1 load description and does not change its voltage, rating, or normal-operation role.
The generic inventory of pull-ups and series resistors adds no value or topology change beyond the candidate's existing main-board pull-up and series-resistor state.
The generic JST connection to LEDs does not specifically change the charge-status LED chain or the separate J_LED_CHG interface.
A main-board JST connection to the sensor board and the absence of sensors on the main board do not change the sensor board's established fanout role.
